title: The UN General Assembly had never had a woman president. Then it did.
sources: United Nations - 1st Woman President of the United Nations General Assembly: Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit
Wikipedia - Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit, UNGA presidency 1953-1954
caption:
The UN General Assembly had never had a woman president. Then it did.

On September 15, 1953, Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit was elected President of the UN General Assembly's 8th session - the first woman in UN history to hold that post. Her term ran to September 1954.

Pandit, sister of Jawaharlal Nehru, had already served as India's ambassador to the United States and the Soviet Union. The UNGA presidency followed years of diplomatic work most of the world never saw.

More than seven decades later, no other Indian has been elected UN General Assembly President. One first, still standing alone, is a reminder that a record isn't the same as a pattern - the next one still has to be built.
